newsitem.title: USA: Crew knew of train's problem before U.S. wreck.
newsitem.headline: Crew knew of train's problem before U.S. wreck.

text.p: Crew members on a CSX Corp. freight train ignored warnings that a truck trailer on a flatcar was leaning because company officials had assured them it posed no danger, the Washington Post reported Friday.
Several cars of the freight train derailed just south of Washington last week, sideswiping an Amtrak passenger train.
The Virginia derailment July 8 slightly injured three Amtrak workers, but the damage it caused will delay regular traffic on the rail route for over a month.
The Post, quoting sources close to the investigation, said CSX supervisors saw that the trailer has shifted but concluded after an inspection that it was safe and decided not to delay the train.
Ninety 90 miles (145 km) later, investigators say, an unbalanced load of heavy paper rolls inside the trailer apparently cause the flatcar to derail.
Crews on passing trains twice radioed warnings about the leaning trailer to the CSX train during the two-hour trip, but the CSX crew replied that company managers had decided it was not a hazard.
A CSX rule requires a train crew to stop and inspect a train after any warning.
